correctness.rationale: Kummer identifies V_t(n) with total p-adic carries. Each fixed low-count event is a finite p-adic digit cylinder. Single-digit carry-run probabilities are exact; disjoint digit ranges yield product coefficients below the minimal gap. At the first possible overlap, a direct two-digit count gives deficit \(d_i d_{i+1}/p^{g+2}\); total-g configurations cannot have multiple overlaps and all other active digits have zero runs. The resulting positive sum proves first-discrepancy at degree g. Exact rational finite-state and complete-period binomial verification reproduced 81 multidigit instances and 8 independent complete-period censuses. The unbounded theorem relies on the proof, not those checks.

value.rationale: The natural fixed-shift valuation distribution is a central prime-adic binomial invariant; its low-valuation fibers are determined by digit amplitudes and spacing. The theorem identifies the precise sharp transition from independent local carry laws to arithmetic dependence and gives the universal first error term, for all digit patterns at every odd prime. This is a structural cutoff and correction, not a renaming, arbitrary finite slice, or a table recomputation. It may support finite precision estimates for binomial divisibility fibers without full transfer-matrix expansions.
